newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 11.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday. IRISH TIMES - Norwich Union's Irish policy holders have borrowed more than 500 million punts to buy the life assurance group's shares ahead of the flotation. - A final draft of a joint document for coalition is expected to be put before the Fianna Fail and Progressive Democrat leaders at the weekend - Overseas buying and strong sterling lifts the Irish pound - Hopes remained high that a last-minute international investment package to save the loss-making container shipping company Bell Lines may emerge IRISH INDEPENDENT - Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats believe they will have their package for government wrapped up by the weekend. - Prime minister-elect Bertie Ahern last night appeared to cast the first doubt on whether Ireland would enter EMU at the starting date in 1999. "I would be for going in but I would be very much watching and trying to have an understanding with the British about what they are going to do," he said. - IFA backs Avonmore-Waterford Foods merger THE EXAMINER - Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern will offer Mary Harney the post of Deputy Prime Minister and a super-junior ministry with the right to attend cabinet meetings. - Bertie Ahern launched his bid to convince the IRA to declare a new ceasefire
